INDUSTRIAL LEASE AGREEMENT

THIS INDUSTRIAL LEASE AGREEMENT ("Lease") is entered into effective as of August 1, 2019 ("Effective Date"), by and between TIDEFLATS LOGISTICS PARK, LLC, a Washington limited liability company ("Landlord"), and MERIDIAN MECHANICAL OF WASHINGTON, LLC, a Washington limited liability company, with a principal place of business at 3310 South Pine Street, Tacoma, Washington 98409 ("Tenant").

RECITALS

WHEREAS, Landlord is the owner of certain real property located at 3310 South Pine Street, Tacoma, Pierce County, Washington, and more particularly described as Lot 1, Block 4, Tideflats Industrial Park, according to the plat thereof recorded in Pierce County, Washington, together with all improvements thereon, parking facilities, and appurtenances (collectively, the "Property"); and

WHEREAS, Landlord desires to lease to Tenant, and Tenant desires to lease from Landlord, a portion of the Property consisting of approximately 16,200 square feet of industrial space on a single floor ("Premises"), all upon the terms and conditions herein contained.

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein and for other good and valuable consideration, Landlord and Tenant agree as follows:

1. PREMISES

1.1 Description and Identification. Landlord hereby leases to Tenant, and Tenant hereby leases from Landlord, the Premises consisting of approximately 16,200 rentable square feet of industrial space located in Building A at 3310 South Pine Street, Tacoma, Washington 98409. The Premises includes the main manufacturing and warehouse space, associated office area of approximately 1,200 square feet, one loading dock with overhead door, one personnel entrance, and designated parking spaces as more particularly described in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. The Premises shall also include access to common areas of the Property, including but not limited to parking areas, driveways, landscaped areas, and pedestrian walkways, all as more particularly shown in Exhibit A.

1.2 Condition of Premises. Tenant acknowledges that it has examined the Premises and accepts the Premises in its current "as is" condition as of the Effective Date, except for those items specifically identified by Landlord as being required to be repaired or remedied prior to commencement of the Term. Tenant's taking possession of the Premises shall constitute acceptance thereof and an acknowledgment that Tenant has received the Premises in good condition and repair, reasonable wear and tear excepted.

1.3 Parking. Tenant shall be entitled to utilize six (6) designated parking spaces located in the common parking area of the Property at no additional charge beyond the Base Rent. Tenant shall not permit its vehicles or the vehicles of its agents, employees, or invitees to park in any area other than the designated spaces or common parking areas designated for Tenant's use, nor shall Tenant permit the obstruction of any parking area, adjoining street, sidewalk, or fire lanes.

1.4 Broker Representation. Tenant represents that it has not dealt with any broker or agent in connection with this Lease and shall be responsible for the full amount of any brokerage commission claimed by any broker with whom Tenant has dealt directly. Landlord represents that it worked with the broker JM Investments Commercial Services in connection with this transaction and shall be responsible for any commission owed to such broker pursuant to a separate agreement.

2. TERM

2.1 Initial Term. The term of this Lease ("Term") shall be for a period of seven (7) years commencing on August 1, 2019 ("Commencement Date") and ending at 11:59 p.m. on July 31, 2026 ("Expiration Date"), unless sooner terminated in accordance with the terms hereof.

2.2 Possession. Tenant shall be entitled to possession of the Premises on the Commencement Date. Rent shall commence to accrue on the Commencement Date regardless of whether Tenant has taken possession of the Premises.

2.3 Renewal Option. Tenant shall have one (1) option to renew this Lease for an additional term of three (3) years ("Renewal Term") on the same terms and conditions as contained in this Lease, except that Base Rent shall be established by mutual agreement of Landlord and Tenant at fair market value for industrial space in the Tideflats Industrial Park area, or if the parties cannot agree within thirty (30) days of Tenant's exercise of this option, at the rate determined by independent appraisal. Tenant must exercise this renewal option, if at all, by providing written notice to Landlord not less than one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the Expiration Date.

3. BASE RENT

3.1 Rent Amount and Payment. Tenant shall pay to Landlord annual Base Rent in monthly installments, payable in advance without demand on the first day of each calendar month during the Term. The monthly Base Rent shall be as follows:

Year 1 (August 1, 2019 through July 31, 2020): $14,580.00 per month
Year 2 (August 1, 2020 through July 31, 2021): $15,017.40 per month
Year 3 (August 1, 2021 through July 31, 2022): $15,467.92 per month
Year 4 (August 1, 2022 through July 31, 2023): $15,932.15 per month
Year 5 (August 1, 2023 through July 31, 2024): $16,410.11 per month
Year 6 (August 1, 2024 through July 31, 2025): $16,902.41 per month
Year 7 (August 1, 2025 through July 31, 2026): $17,409.49 per month

Annual escalations of three percent (3%) shall be compounded annually on each anniversary of the Commencement Date.

3.2 Rent Payment Address and Method. All rent payments shall be made payable to "Tideflats Logistics Park, LLC" and delivered to: Tideflats Logistics Park, LLC, P.O. Box 8847, Tacoma, Washington 98408, Attention: Property Management, or to such other address as Landlord may designate in writing. Rent may be paid by check, electronic transfer, or such other method as Landlord may authorize.

3.3 Late Payment. Rent not received by Landlord within five (5) days after it is due shall be deemed late. Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the overdue payment. Additionally, Tenant shall pay interest on any overdue amount at the rate of twelve percent (12%) per annum from the due date until paid, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is less. The acceptance of a late payment shall not constitute a waiver of Tenant's default or of Landlord's right to enforce any provision of this Lease.

3.4 No Abatement of Rent. Except as may be expressly provided herein, Tenant shall pay rent for the entire Term without deduction, offset, or abatement, regardless of any defect, casualty, condemnation, or other circumstances affecting the Premises or the Property.

3.5 Additional Rent. In addition to Base Rent, Tenant shall pay all charges, costs, and expenses as Additional Rent, including but not limited to Tenant's proportionate share of real estate taxes and common area maintenance costs as set forth in Section 7 hereof, utilities as set forth in Section 8 hereof, insurance premiums as required in Section 6 hereof, and any other charges that become due and payable during the Term.

4. USE OF PREMISES

4.1 Permitted Use. The Premises shall be used solely and exclusively for the operation of a mechanical contracting business, including but not limited to the performance of plumbing and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system installation, maintenance, and repair services, warehousing of materials and equipment related to such business, office and administrative functions, and for such other purposes as may be incidental to the foregoing business. Tenant shall not use the Premises for any other purpose without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed.

4.2 Compliance with Law. Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, codes, ordinances, regulations, and requirements, including but not limited to the building code, fire code, safety regulations, environmental regulations, zoning ordinances, and all applicable licensing requirements related to the use and operation of the Premises. Tenant shall obtain and maintain all necessary licenses, permits, and certifications required for the lawful operation of its business. Tenant shall be responsible for all costs associated with compliance with law as it relates to Tenant's use and occupancy of the Premises.

4.3 Prohibited Activities. Tenant shall not use or permit the Premises to be used for any unlawful purpose or in any manner that would violate this Lease or any applicable law. Tenant shall not use the Premises for manufacturing (other than assembly and repair related to Tenant's contracting business), storage of hazardous materials in quantities exceeding those reasonably necessary for Tenant's daily operations, or for any use that would create a nuisance or materially interfere with the quiet enjoyment of the Property by other tenants or neighbors.

4.4 Hazardous Materials. Tenant shall not bring into, store, use, or permit the presence of any hazardous substances or wastes in or about the Premises except in ordinary quantities necessary for the operation of Tenant's business, such as cleaning supplies, refrigerants, solvents, and fuels in sealed containers. Tenant shall immediately notify Landlord of any spill, leak, or release of any hazardous substance and shall promptly remediate any such release at Tenant's sole cost and expense in compliance with all applicable laws.

5. MAINTENANCE AND REPAIRS

5.1 Tenant's Maintenance Obligations. Tenant shall be responsible for and shall promptly perform all maintenance, repair, and replacement of all systems, fixtures, and equipment within the Premises, including but not limited to heating and air conditioning systems, fixtures and equipment, dock equipment, loading dock doors and areas, roof (interior surface), interior walls, interior doors, floors and floor slab, electrical systems, plumbing systems, fire protection systems, light fixtures, ceiling and ceiling systems, and all other systems, fixtures, machinery, apparatus, equipment, and appurtenances now or hereafter part of, belonging to, connected with, or used in conjunction with the Premises.

5.2 Quality of Repairs. All repairs and replacements shall be of first-class quality and sufficient for the proper maintenance and operation of the Premises. Tenant shall obtain competitive bids for all repairs exceeding $5,000 and shall submit such bids to Landlord for its approval prior to commencing any work. Tenant shall use qualified, licensed contractors for all major repairs and maintenance. All repairs shall be completed in a professional and timely manner and shall comply with all applicable building codes and regulations.

5.3 Janitorial and Sanitation. Tenant shall keep and maintain the Premises in a clean, orderly, safe, and secure condition at all times, specifically including but not limited to the prompt and regular removal of all waste, refuse matter, and debris. Tenant shall maintain adequate waste disposal containers and shall arrange for regular removal of trash at Tenant's sole cost and expense. Tenant shall keep the interior of the Premises clean and free of pests, vermin, and rodents.

5.4 Parking Area and Common Areas. Tenant shall keep all parking areas designated for its use clear and unobstructed and shall not permit vehicles to be parked in any restricted or fire lane areas. Tenant shall not obstruct or permit the obstruction of any adjoining street, sidewalk, loading areas, or fire lanes. Tenant shall immediately report to Landlord any damage to common areas caused by Tenant or its agents, employees, or invitees.

5.5 Preventive Maintenance. Tenant shall perform regular preventive maintenance on all systems serving the Premises to prevent breakdowns and emergencies. Tenant shall maintain a log of all maintenance activities and shall provide copies to Landlord upon request.

5.6 Landlord's Maintenance Obligations. Landlord shall be responsible for the maintenance and repair of the exterior roof (exterior surface only), exterior walls and structural elements, foundation, fire protection systems serving the entire building, common area lighting, common area landscaping, common area parking lot surface, and other common area elements. Landlord shall also maintain adequate snow and ice removal on the common parking areas and common driveways, except that Tenant shall be responsible for snow and ice removal on its loading dock area and the area immediately adjacent thereto.

5.7 Emergency Repairs. In the event of an emergency requiring immediate repair to prevent damage to the Premises or the Property, Tenant may engage a contractor and proceed with emergency repairs without first obtaining Landlord's approval, provided that Tenant shall give Landlord notice of such emergency within twenty-four (24) hours and shall provide documentation of the emergency and the repairs completed.

6. INSURANCE

6.1 Tenant's Insurance Requirements. Tenant shall obtain and maintain, at Tenant's sole cost and expense, comprehensive general liability insurance covering the Premises with minimum coverage of Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) per occurrence and Four Million Dollars ($4,000,000) aggregate. Tenant shall also maintain property insurance covering all of Tenant's equipment, fixtures, inventory, and other personal property located in the Premises with a minimum coverage of the full replacement value thereof.

6.2 Property Insurance. Tenant shall maintain property insurance covering all fixtures, equipment, alterations, and improvements installed by Tenant in the Premises. Such insurance shall name Landlord as an additional insured and loss payee and shall provide that it cannot be cancelled without thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Landlord.

6.3 Workers' Compensation. Tenant shall maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by the laws of the State of Washington, with minimum limits as prescribed by law.

6.4 Insurance Certificates. Tenant shall provide Landlord with certificates of insurance evidencing the required coverage prior to the Commencement Date and shall provide updated certificates annually and upon renewal of any policy. All insurance policies shall provide that coverage shall not be modified or cancelled without thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Landlord.

6.5 Insurance Not Limitation of Liability. Tenant's maintenance of insurance shall not limit Tenant's indemnification obligations or liability under this Lease. The requirement that Tenant maintain insurance shall not be deemed to satisfy Tenant's obligation to indemnify and hold harmless Landlord.

6.6 No Insurance on Premises. Landlord shall maintain no insurance on the Premises or building. Tenant shall insure all of its property and operations. Loss or damage to Tenant's property shall be Tenant's responsibility regardless of the cause.

7. TAXES AND COMMON AREA MAINTENANCE

7.1 Real Estate Taxes. Tenant shall pay Tenant's proportionate share of all real estate taxes and assessments levied on the Property. Tenant's proportionate share shall be calculated based on the ratio of the rentable square footage of the Premises (16,200 square feet) to the total rentable square footage of the Property (approximately 48,600 square feet), which represents approximately 33.33% of the Property. Tenant's share of taxes for the first year is estimated at $400 per month, payable as Additional Rent, subject to adjustment based on actual tax assessments.

7.2 Common Area Maintenance. Beginning on August 1, 2019 and for the remainder of the Term, Tenant shall be responsible for and shall pay Tenant's proportionate share (33.33%) of the costs for common area maintenance and repair at the Property, including but not limited to landscaping and grounds maintenance, fire alarm monitoring and maintenance, sprinkler system maintenance, snow and ice removal from the common parking lot and common driveways, parking lot surface maintenance and repair, common area lighting and exterior lighting maintenance, common area cleaning, and all other common area costs. Tenant's share of estimated common area maintenance for the first year is estimated at $300 per month, payable as Additional Rent, subject to adjustment based on actual costs and a true-up accounting annually.

7.3 Calculation and Adjustment. Landlord shall provide Tenant with an estimate of Additional Rent charges related to taxes and common area maintenance annually, which estimate shall be divided equally among all tenants of the Property (or on a square footage basis as appropriate). Tenant shall pay the estimated amount monthly. Within ninety (90) days following the end of each calendar year, Landlord shall provide Tenant with a statement of actual costs and charges. If Tenant has overpaid, the overpayment shall be credited against future rent due. If Tenant has underpaid, Tenant shall pay the shortfall within ten (10) days of invoice.

8. UTILITIES

Tenant shall be responsible for and shall pay for all utilities serving the Premises, including but not limited to electricity, natural gas, water, sewer, telephone, and Internet services. Utilities shall be separately metered to the Premises where practicable, and Tenant shall arrange for all utilities to be billed directly to Tenant. If utilities are not separately metered, Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for Tenant's proportionate share of utility costs based on the ratio of rentable square footage or such other method as may be agreed by Landlord and Tenant.

9. DEFAULT AND REMEDIES

9.1 Events of Default. Tenant shall be in default of this Lease upon the occurrence of any one or more of the following events:

(a) If Tenant fails to pay any rent or other charge due hereunder when due and such failure continues for five (5) business days after written notice from Landlord;

(b) If Tenant fails to comply with any other material provision of this Lease and such failure continues for fifteen (15) days after written notice from Landlord, or if such default cannot reasonably be cured within fifteen (15) days, Tenant fails to commence cure within such period and diligently pursue such cure to completion within a reasonable time not to exceed thirty (30) days;

(c) If Tenant abandons the Premises or ceases operations therein for a period of thirty (30) consecutive days;

(d) If any of Tenant's personal property or equipment is levied upon by legal process and such levy is not released within thirty (30) days;

(e) If Tenant files for bankruptcy, insolvency, or receivership, or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or if such proceedings are filed against Tenant and not dismissed within ninety (90) days;

(f) If Tenant materially violates the use restrictions or other material terms of this Lease.

9.2 Landlord's Remedies. Upon the occurrence of any default by Tenant and the expiration of any applicable notice and cure period, Landlord shall have the right, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity:

(a) To terminate this Lease and re-enter and repossess the Premises without court proceedings if entry can be made without a breach of the peace;

(b) To sue for and recover all rent and other charges due through the date of re-entry, plus all rent and charges that would have been due for the remainder of the Term, less a reasonable allowance for Landlord's costs of reletting;

(c) To perform any obligations of Tenant hereunder, and Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for all costs and expenses so incurred, including reasonable attorneys' fees, within ten (10) days of invoice;

(d) To pursue any and all other remedies at law or in equity without limiting any other right or remedy available to Landlord.

9.3 Late Charges and Default Interest. In addition to any other remedy, Tenant shall pay a late charge of five percent (5%) of any overdue amount, plus interest at twelve percent (12%) per annum on all past due amounts, or the maximum rate permitted by law.

9.4 Attorney's Fees. In the event Landlord prevails in any action or proceeding relating to this Lease or the enforcement thereof, Tenant shall reimburse Landlord for all reasonable attorney's fees, court costs, and other legal expenses incurred by Landlord.

9.5 Waiver. The failure of Landlord to enforce any provision of this Lease or to exercise any right or remedy upon default shall not constitute a waiver of such provision, right, or remedy, nor shall it operate as a waiver of any subsequent default.

10. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBLETTING

10.1 Restriction on Assignment. Tenant shall not assign, transfer, or encumber this Lease or sublet the Premises or any part thereof without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. Any attempted assignment or subletting without such consent shall be void and shall constitute a material default of this Lease.

10.2 Conditions to Consent. If Tenant requests Landlord's consent to assign this Lease or sublet the Premises, Tenant shall provide Landlord with detailed information regarding the proposed assignee or subtenant, including financial information and business background. Landlord shall have ten (10) business days to approve or object to the proposed assignment or subletting. If Landlord consents to an assignment, Tenant shall remain liable for the full performance of this Lease unless expressly released by Landlord in writing.

10.3 Assignment Premium. If Tenant assigns this Lease at a profit (i.e., the rent received by Tenant exceeds the rent payable by Tenant under this Lease), Tenant shall pay Landlord fifty percent (50%) of such profit.

11. INDEMNIFICATION

11.1 Tenant's Indemnity. Tenant shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Landlord, the owners of the Property, and their respective officers, directors, employees, and agents from and against all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, and expenses (including reasonable attorney's fees) arising out of or related to: (a) Tenant's use or occupancy of the Premises; (b) any breach of this Lease by Tenant; (c) any injury to persons or damage to property occurring within or about the Premises caused by Tenant, its employees, agents, or invitees; (d) Tenant's failure to comply with applicable law; or (e) the discharge or release of any hazardous substance caused by Tenant.

11.2 Landlord's Indemnity. Landlord shall indemnify Tenant against all claims arising out of Landlord's gross negligence or willful misconduct in connection with the maintenance of the common areas or the structural elements of the building.

12. COMPLIANCE WITH APPLICABLE LAW

12.1 General Compliance. Tenant shall comply with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, statutes, ordinances, codes, rules, regulations, and requirements, including but not limited to building codes, fire codes, plumbing codes, electrical codes, OSHA regulations, EPA requirements, and all other laws relating to the use and occupancy of the Premises or the conduct of Tenant's business.

12.2 Governmental Requirements. Tenant shall, at its sole cost and expense, promptly comply with any and all governmental requirements imposed by any governmental entity affecting the Premises or any part thereof as a result of Tenant's use and occupancy, irrespective of whether such requirements involve structural changes or alterations to the Premises.

12.3 ADA Compliance. Tenant shall comply with the Americans with Disabilities Act and all applicable accessibility requirements in the use and operation of the Premises.

13. FIRE EXTINGUISHERS AND SAFETY EQUIPMENT

Tenant shall obtain and maintain fire extinguishers, first aid kits, and all other safety equipment as required by applicable law and fire code in the Premises at Tenant's sole cost and expense. Tenant shall ensure that all safety equipment is properly maintained and inspected according to legal requirements and shall immediately report any deficiencies to Landlord.

14. ENTRY AND INSPECTION

14.1 Right of Entry. Landlord shall have the right to enter the Premises during normal business hours upon at least twenty-four (24) hours' prior notice to Tenant (except in emergencies) for the purpose of inspecting the Premises, showing the Premises to prospective tenants during the final twelve (12) months of the Term, making repairs for which Landlord is responsible, or otherwise managing the Property.

14.2 Emergency Entry. In the event of an emergency such as fire, flood, or other immediate threat to the safety of persons or property, Landlord may enter the Premises without notice.

15. TENANT IMPROVEMENTS

Any alterations, additions, or improvements to the Premises shall be the responsibility of Tenant. Tenant shall not make any alterations or improvements to the Premises without the prior written consent of Landlord, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld for non-structural alterations that do not affect the building systems or exterior. All alterations and improvements shall be performed in a professional manner by licensed contractors and shall comply with all building codes and regulations.

16. SURRENDER OF PREMISES

Upon expiration or earlier termination of this Lease, Tenant shall immediately vacate the Premises and shall return the Premises to Landlord in clean condition, free of all of Tenant's personal property and debris. Tenant shall remove all fixtures and equipment installed by Tenant (unless otherwise agreed), repair any damage caused by such removal, and leave the Premises in good condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted. Failure to vacate shall result in holdover rent equal to 150% of the monthly Base Rent.

17. ENTIRE AGREEMENT

This Lease, including all exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between Landlord and Tenant regarding the leasing of the Premises and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, and agreements. No modification or amendment to this Lease shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by both Landlord and Tenant.

18. SEVERABILITY

If any provision of this Lease is found to be invalid or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction, such provision shall be severed and all other provisions shall remain in full force and effect.

19. GOVERNING LAW AND JURISDICTION

This Lease shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Washington, without regard to its conflict of law provisions. Any legal action or proceeding relating to this Lease shall be brought exclusively in the state courts located in Pierce County, Washington, and Tenant consents to the jurisdiction and venue of such courts.

20. NOTICES

Any notice required or permitted hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed given when delivered personally, sent by email with confirmation of receipt, sent by overnight courier, or sent by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the addresses set forth below:

To Landlord:
Tideflats Logistics Park, LLC
P.O. Box 8847
Tacoma, Washington 98408
Attention: Property Management
Email: property@tideflatslogistics.com

To Tenant:
Meridian Mechanical of Washington, LLC
3310 South Pine Street
Tacoma, Washington 98409
Attention: Manager
Email: office@meridianmechanical.com

21. WAIVER OF JURY TRIAL

EACH PARTY HEREBY WAIVES ANY RIGHT TO TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION OR PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF THIS LEASE.

22. AUTHORITY

Each party represents and warrants to the other that it has full power and authority to enter into this Lease and that the person executing this Lease on its behalf is duly authorized to do so.

23. TIME OF ESSENCE

Time is of the essence in this Lease. All dates and time periods specified herein are material to the rights and obligations of the parties.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, Landlord and Tenant have executed this Lease as of the date first written above.
